label: IPv6 Fragment Header
notes: IPv6 Fragment extension header (next header 44) per RFC 8200 section 4.5: the fixed 8-byte header only. The anchor assumes the fragment header directly follows the 40-byte IPv6 header, the common single-extension layout; extension headers chained in front of it shift every offset, and the ip6 proto locator matches anywhere in the chain. Bytes 2-3 are one bit-packed word carrying three masked views: the 13-bit Fragment Offset, the 2-bit Res and the 1-bit M flag, each compiled as its own clause. The fragmentable part follows byte 8: the first fragment repeats the rest of the original packet's header chain there while later fragments carry pure payload, so nothing past the header sits at a trustworthy fixed offset. Offset 0 with M=0 marks an unfragmented packet that still carries the header, the atomic fragment of RFC 6946; first fragments are offset 0 with M=1. All 8 header bytes are covered by field views; the entry has no excluded bytes.

fields.label: Next Header
fields.description: Type of the header immediately following the Fragment Header in the original packet.

fields.label: Reserved
fields.description: Reserved byte; transmitted as zero and ignored on reception.

fields.label: Fragment Offset
fields.description: Offset in 8-octet units from the start of the fragmentable part of the original packet to the first octet of this fragment; 154 means byte 1232, one 1280-MTU hop.

fields.label: Res
fields.description: Two reserved bits between the Fragment Offset and the M flag; transmitted as zero.

fields.label: More Fragments
fields.description: 1 when more fragments follow; 0 marks the last fragment. Offset 0 with M=0 is the unfragmented atomic-fragment idiom of RFC 6946.

fields.label: Identification
fields.description: 32-bit value shared by every fragment of the same original packet, set by the sender.
